title: Audio interface
intro: Which input records the turntable, and in which format. Changes apply from the next recording or level check, without a restart.
device_help: Automatic takes an audio interface with at least two inputs (an ASIO driver first, then USB), never a microphone or a virtual device.
profile_wins: The active turntable profile “{name}” records from {device}; the profile's device takes precedence over this one.
rate_help: 48 kHz is what the click detection was tuned at. 96 kHz doubles the file size (192 kHz: four times). Grades are best compared at the same rate.
rate_switch: The interface runs at {now} kHz now. vinyl-check switches it to {rate} kHz while recording; other programs using it will notice.
rate_shared: In WASAPI shared mode Windows records at the rate set in its sound settings ({now} kHz). Another rate needs exclusive mode.
rate_unknown: Which rates this device supports cannot be read without opening it. The test shows whether the rate works.
bits_help: 24 bit leaves headroom for setting levels and lowers the noise floor of the alignment measurements. Devices that only offer 16 bit (most USB turntables) record at 16 bit.
inputs_help: The two inputs of the interface the turntable or the phono stage is connected to.
inputs_test_file: Test mode: the test file is played back as it is, so the choice of inputs does not apply.
exclusive_help: Records straight from the converter, past the Windows mixer and its effects; other programs cannot use the input meanwhile. Without it, or if the device does not allow it, Windows records in shared mode at the format set in its sound settings.
asio_help: Interfaces with an ASIO driver are listed first and chosen automatically: the most direct path to the converter. WASAPI serves devices without one. Off: WASAPI only.
asio_unavailable: Not available: this installation has no ASIO build of PortAudio.
asio_restart: Restart vinyl-check to load the ASIO drivers.
source_device: Follows the device; saving keeps it fixed.
saved: Audio settings saved. They apply from the next recording or level check.
reset_confirm: Remove the audio settings made here? The configuration file and the defaults apply again.
reset_done: The audio settings made here were removed.
test_hint: Opens the device with these settings for one second, without saving them and without recording.
test_silent: The inputs are silent. Play a record, or check the input pair and the level.
test_clip: Clipping: lower the level on the interface or the phono stage.
locked: A recording or level check is running. The audio settings can be changed afterwards.
service_hint: Settings made under Audio interface take precedence over these values. Everything else is in {file} and cannot be changed here because the service may not write there; restart the service after changing the file.
service_hint_desktop: Recording device, sample rate, bit depth and inputs are set under Audio interface above. For advanced settings vinyl-check also reads {file} (create it if it does not exist, then quit and reopen vinyl-check); settings made in the interface take precedence.
